title: James Peak low-water scouting hypotheses
occupancy_assumption: User assumes elk occupancy in 2027; model does not estimate occupancy or harvest probability.
scenario: Low surface water: prioritize mapped perennial water over seasonal or unknown classes. No future discharge, water-level or drought prediction is made.

water.meaning: Distance and mapped permanence of nearest selected stream/lake
water.description: Natural mapped streams, non-ice lake/pond polygons and spring/seep points only. Artificial paths, connectors, ditches, pipelines, glaciers, marsh polygons and gate points are excluded. Historical NHD classifications do not establish 2027 flow. No lake-volume, groundwater or streamflow simulation.

shelter.meaning: Percent tree canopy cover at the point
shelter.description: Higher canopy reaches a saturated score at 70%; candidate admission requires at least 30%. Overhead vegetation is a proxy, not a field assessment of bedding, understory, visibility or live-tree condition.

darkness.meaning: Distance to nearest mapped trail, road, or developed campground
darkness.description: Geometric separation from mapped access, not measured human use, solitude, night lighting, or hunting pressure.
darkness.overlay_units: Meters from nearest mapped trail, road or developed campground; 0–2000 m display, saturated beyond 2000 m.

security.meaning: Nearby steep terrain around an accessible local slope
security.description: Intermediate nearby steep terrain around a gentler cell is treated as a reconnaissance cue. Extremely extensive steep terrain is discounted. This heuristic is unvalidated; true pinch points, ingress/egress, elk escape routes and line of sight are not derived.
security.formula: Let f be fraction of cells with averaged slope >=25 degrees within a 200 m disk. score = 100*min(clip(f/0.35,0,1),clip((0.85-f)/0.30,0,1))*clip((35-local_slope_degrees)/20,0,1).

selection.nearby_pool: Up to six highest-scoring spatially separated candidates with geodesic distance <=3 miles from East Portal. This is a necessary distance screen, not route validation.
selection.wilderness_context_pool: Up to ten highest-scoring remaining cells, excluding 400 m around nearby candidates; no duplicate neighborhoods between pools.
selection.exact_geometry_rechecks: Exact vector distance admission checks for candidate water and access; all other scores are 60 m raster estimates.

route_limits.vehicle: AWD Mazda3, no high clearance required
route_limits.reason: A geodesic lower bound over 3 mi means any out-and-back to East Portal exceeds 6 mi; shorter straight-line distances do not prove a feasible route. Cumulative ascent is not calculated.

required_field_checks: Fresh elk sign and dated camera detections
Actual foot route and cumulative elevation
Human use and unmapped dispersed camps
interpretation: Perfect spots is the user-facing layer label. Points are ranked reconnaissance hypotheses, not confirmed perfect habitat or promises.

canopy_source.dataset: USFS NLCD Percent Tree Canopy CONUS v2025-6
canopy_source.model_resampling: Bilinear to 60 m modeling grid; candidate values are local model-grid estimates, not raw source-pixel integers.

distance_uncertainty: Distance rasters use 60 m cells, all-touched source geometry and Euclidean distance transform; raster distances are approximate and can differ by about a cell from exact vector distances. Candidate water_distance_m and nearest_access_m are exact vector distances; component scores retain the continuous raster model.

source_vintages.water: Legacy USGS NHD High Resolution; retired 2023 and retained as historical mapped hydrography
source_vintages.canopy: 2025 mapped year, official v2025-6 product released 2026
source_vintages.elevation: USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second DEM, resampled for modeling
source_vintages.access: USFS and The National Map snapshot; completeness and current use not established
source_vintages.ownership: PAD-US fee ownership and USFS wilderness boundary snapshot
